chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah who said:

I asked him about the slave who fabricates (accuses falsely) upon the free man. He said: 'He is whipped eighty (lashes)'. I said: 'So if he committed adultery?' He said: 'He is whipped fifty (lashes)'.

key_terms.الْمَمْلُوكِ: The slave (owned person), specifically in the context of hadd punishments

ai.seo_question: What is the penalty for a slave who commits adultery or false accusation according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi details the specific hadd punishments for a slave (mamluk), establishing eighty lashes for false accusation (qadhf) and fifty for adultery (zina). These figures represent half the standard penalties for a free person, reflecting the jurisprudential principle that slaves receive reduced corporal punishment due to their status. The narration highlights the practical application of these legal distinctions within Shia fiqh.
